98f2b877ee.substituent_description: Bicyclic 5-6 fused system: a five-membered ring containing an N (top left) fused to a six-membered pyridine-type ring containing one ring N at the top right. The five-ring N carries Ac; the adjacent five-ring carbon carries EtOOC; the next five-ring carbon is an unsubstituted CH2 vertex. On the six-ring, the carbon directly next to the ring N (top right) carries OMe (pyridine N and OMe carbon are adjacent, 1,2 relationship).
98f2b877ee.notes: Typeset drawing. Three double bonds in the six-membered ring: one C=C at the top-left next to the fusion, one C=N at the right, one C=C at the bottom. The five-membered ring has only single bonds. No stereo bonds drawn at the EtOOC-bearing carbon.

fa07a7f70b.substituent_description: A six-membered ring drawn as a hexagon with a small circle inside. It carries OPh at the upper-right vertex and, para to it (lower-left vertex), a CH2 vertex leading to a chain carbon. That chain carbon bears MeOOC through a hashed bond and is bonded by a plain line straight up to NHBoc (so the chain is ring-CH2-CH(MeOOC, hashed)-NHBoc).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The final C of MeOOC is written like an open 'c'/alpha shape and the OO look like open circles, so the label is read as MeOOC with slight doubt.
A dark ink blob sits on the lower-right ring vertex and could be mistaken for a wedge but looks like a pen blot.
The 'h' of OPh is written like a lowercase 'h' with a long ascender.
fa07a7f70b.notes: Handwritten, black pen on white paper. The aromatic ring is shown with a small hand-drawn circle (no alternating double bonds). The hashed bond is a set of about 5-6 short strokes between the stereocentre and MeOOC.

968ab97411.substituent_description: A six-membered ring with two adjacent ring N atoms at the top (N-N bond) and a circle inside is fused to a five-membered ring with two more N atoms; the five-ring has an explicit N=CH double bond at lower left and an N at lower right. The six-ring carbon at the far left bears NH2 (drawn as H, N, H stacked vertically); the six-ring carbon at the right bears COO-C(CH3)3 (tert-butyl ester written as COO, a C label and three CH3). The lower-right five-ring N is attached through a solid wedge to a cyclohexane ring; on the cyclohexane, the carbon adjacent to the wedge carbon carries BocNH via a hashed bond, and the carbon on the opposite side of the ring (1,4 to the wedge carbon) carries a hashed bond to a CH2 vertex followed by CO2H.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: NH2 on the left is written as three stacked characters H / N / H with short bonds between them.
The hashed bond at the bottom of the cyclohexane ends at an unlabelled vertex, then a plain line goes to CO2H, so the group reads as CH2CO2H.
Wedge on the upper cyclohexane carbon is wide at the heteroaryl N end and narrow at the ring carbon.
968ab97411.notes: Handwritten black pen. One small circle inside the six-membered aza-ring (circle depiction) while the five-membered ring shows one explicit double bond (N=CH), hence both. Four ring N atoms are labelled. Cyclohexane ring has no other double bonds.

4be595da7b.substituent_description: From left to right: a pyrrolidine ring whose N is bonded to a C(=O) carbonyl (urea), then NH, then CH2CH2 to one N of a piperazine ring; the other piperazine N is bonded to a para-disubstituted benzene ring whose para position carries O-CH2 leading (via a hashed bond) to C4 of a 1,3-dioxolane ring. The dioxolane C2 (quaternary carbon between its two ring O atoms) bears a 2,4-dichlorophenyl ring (Cl ortho and Cl para to the attachment point) and, via a hashed bond to a CH2, an imidazol-1-yl ring (N-linked).
4be595da7b.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: 1 C=O, 3 in the central phenylene, 3 in the dichlorophenyl, 2 in the imidazole (C=N and C=C). Two hashed wedges, no solid wedges, no written stereo labels.

44593476fa.substituent_description: Left: a bicyclic pyrrole-fused pyrimidinone: the pyrrole N carries Me, the pyrrole carbon next to it carries I, the pyrimidine ring has a ring N at the top, a C=O at the bottom and a ring N (right) bonded to a CH2. That CH2 is attached to C4 of a first piperidine ring, which also carries HO on the same carbon (4-hydroxy-4-CH2-piperidine); its ring N is acylated by a C(=O). The carbonyl carbon is attached by a solid wedge to C4 of a second piperidine ring, whose adjacent C3 bears Ph via a hashed bond and whose ring N bears Boc.
44593476fa.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: C=N and C=C (shared fusion bond) and C=C in the bicyclic core, C=O on the pyrimidinone ring, and the amide C=O. Solid wedge is narrow at the second piperidine ring carbon; hashed bond to Ph is narrow at the ring carbon.

2fe459ecfd.substituent_description: Left benzene ring (circle) is para-disubstituted: AcNH at one end and a sulfonyl S (two S=O, drawn above and below) at the other. S is bonded to N, which carries a line that bends and ends at 'Bn' and also a CH2 vertex leading to a C(=O) (O drawn above), then NH, then N=CH (C=N double bond) ending at a five-membered ring. The five-membered ring has one N labelled, two ring double bonds, one methyl stub on each carbon flanking the N, and the CH= attached to the ring carbon adjacent to one of the methyl-bearing carbons (i.e. 2,5-dimethylpyrrol-3-yl). The ring N is bonded to a benzene ring (circle) carrying a methyl stub ortho and a methyl stub para to the N attachment (2,4-dimethylphenyl).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The line from the sulfonamide N goes up, bends, then runs to 'Bn', so there is an extra unlabelled vertex between N and Bn.
Methyl groups on the pyrrole and aryl rings are drawn as bare line stubs with no label.
The pyrrole ring has only one labelled heteroatom (N).
2fe459ecfd.notes: Handwritten black pen. 6 double bonds: two S=O, one C=O, one N=CH, two in the five-membered ring. Both six-membered rings use a hand-drawn circle; the five-membered ring uses explicit double bonds. Stacked NH labels (N over H) on the hydrazide are recorded as NH.

55a55602dd.substituent_description: Central five-membered ring with three N atoms and an exocyclic C=O: one ring N (left) is bonded to a benzene ring bearing Cl para to the attachment point; one ring N is NH; the ring carbon opposite the C=O carries an NH linker to a second benzene ring that has CO2H para to the NH attachment. A C=N double bond is in the five-membered ring.
55a55602dd.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: 1 C=O, 1 ring C=N, 3 in the chlorophenyl ring, 3 in the benzoic acid ring. The linking NH has its H drawn below the N.

21a13e4218.substituent_description: A spiro carbon joins a pyrrolidine ring (ring N bearing Boc) and a five-membered lactam ring (C=O above, ring N to the right). The lactam ring is fused to a six-membered ring with one ring N (drawn at the lower right, adjacent to the carbon bonded to the lactam N). The lactam N carries a CH2 attached to a benzene ring (circle) that has OMe para to the CH2 attachment.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Spiro carbon is drawn as four lines meeting at one point (crossing look).
The C=N bond in the six-membered ring is drawn as a short inner stroke rather than a full parallel line.
21a13e4218.notes: Handwritten black pen. 4 double bonds: lactam C=O plus 3 in the pyridine ring (alternating style). The benzyl ring uses a hand-drawn circle.
